title: Adaptive epoch alignment for tenant quota watermarks and reserved burst reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Customers on reserved capacity and rolling-window quotas have seen intermittent double-charging and lost allowance events during aligned resets (monthly/day boundary) and during tenant timezone rollovers. Root causes observed in the last incidents: (1) race between epoch reset job and in-flight token accrual, (2) misaligned reset anchors for tenants with tenant-specific timezone offsets, and (3) fallback to legacy burst buckets that were not reconciled after failover.

Goal:
Introduce an "adaptive epoch alignment" approach that: (a) provides an idempotent reset mechanism using per-tenant watermarks, (b) uses short-lived lease handoff for in-flight counters to avoid double-applies, (c) performs probabilistic jittered resets to avoid thundering-herd on month/day boundaries, and (d) adds a reconciliation backfill job for reserved-capacity burst buckets to guarantee eventual correctness and auditable corrections.

High level design:
1) Quota epochs: add a tenant_quota_epoch (UTC timestamp) and tenant_quota_watermark ( opaque reset token ) to the quota table. Resets advance epoch via compare-and-swap; the watermark is rotated atomically so repeated reset attempts are idempotent.
2) Lease-based in-flight protection: when a request mutates a tenant's counters, it obtains a short Redis/Etcd lease keyed by tenant+epoch. If a reset wins the CAS, it waits for the lease TTL window (configurable, default 3s) before committing the reset, or attempts a safe offset merge.
3) Probabilistic jitter: slate-of-reset workers pick tenant reset times within a small jitter window (symmetric +/- jitter) derived from tenant id hash to smooth load spikes. An emergency run-forced path exists for tenants flagged by billing anomalies.
4) Reserved burst reconciliation: background job scans reserved buckets for mismatches between persistent usage and billing ledger and emits corrective ledger adjustments (audit-only by default, then auto-apply with flag). Backfill window defaults to 30 days and is tunable.

Schema & migrations:
- add columns: tenant_quota_epoch (TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE), tenant_quota_watermark (VARCHAR), quota_last_mutation_id (UUID)
- migration plan: online add columns with no lock, backfill epoch for active tenants to nearest midnight-aligned epoch, then flip feature flag to use new path.

Operational considerations:
- Strong consistency tradeoff: we avoid global locks to preserve throughput; choice is eventual correctness with an audit trail + corrective job. This minimizes latency/regression to token throughput but requires reconciliation when edge cases occur.
- Observability: add metrics: quota_reset_attempts, quota_reset_success, quota_reset_conflicts, lease_wait_time_seconds, reserved_reconcile_actions, reconcile_latency_histogram. Dashboards and alerts to be added.
- Backwards compat: legacy tenants continue to be served by existing counters until migration cutoff; all resets are logged to the billing audit stream for replay.

Testing plan:
- unit tests for CAS and watermark rotation logic
- integration tests simulating concurrent mutators + reset workers with deterministic pseudo-random jitter seeds
- chaos tests introducing clock skew and lease failures
- load test to validate throughput impact at 10k RPS across tenant set

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy migration and feature flag off. Backfill epoch for a small set (canary) of low-volume tenants.
2) Enable feature flag for canary tenants, monitor metrics for 48h.
3) Gradually expand canary cohort; tune lease TTL and jitter window.
4) Enable for all tenants; start reserved reconciliation in audit-only mode for 7 days, review corrections.
5) Flip auto-apply for corrections after SRE/Finance signoff.

- Confluence design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Epoch+Alignment (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4987 (WIP)

comments: 2026-02-19 — Aisha: Created ticket after postmortem for incident INC-2026-02-17. Initial design sketch attached to Confluence. Prioritized as P0 because billing discrepancies affected several enterprise tenants.

2026-02-22 — Marco: Spike completed for lease-based approach. Findings: Redis lease works but increases tail latency by ~0.8ms for mutating calls under 99.9th percentile. Recommend default TTL 3s and place feature behind runtime flag for tuning.

2026-02-25 — Eng review: Architecture review with Storage and Billing teams. Key feedback: ensure reconcile job writes audit-only corrections first and requires Finance sign-off before auto-apply. Also add an immutable reset_id in ledger for traceability.

2026-02-28 — PR opened: #4987. Code review comments requested stricter guardrails around migration backfill to avoid scanning hot tenant tables during business hours. Action: implement paginated backfill with rate limit.

2026-03-01 — QA: Integration tests added for concurrent reset + mutator scenarios. Found a race in watermark rotation when two reset workers concurrently attempt CAS — fixed by including epoch and rotation counter in CAS key.

2026-03-02 — Blocker noted: Platform infra team needs to expose a high-availability Redis namespace for short-lived leases; blocked until infra ticket INFRA-6223 is completed. Escalated to infra lead.

2026-03-03 — Marco: Added dashboards for quota_reset_conflicts and lease_wait_time_seconds. Started canary backfill for 50 tenants in eu-west-1 in audit-only mode. No corrections auto-applied yet. Monitoring OK.
2026-03-03 — Next steps: finish migration rate-limiter, resolve INFRA-6223, and schedule cross-team review with Finance for reconcile auto-apply policy.
